head: d79ce1426da05a05a04ff1dc8c1c0197a862eecc
summary:
Criterion 1 is built as designed, and I ran it. DefenderState.cs reads Controlled Folder Access through a 5.1 child with PSModulePath removed, async reads, a 20 s timeout and a process-tree kill. Describe never throws, and HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() writes the line straight after the fsutil line. Under eng/dotnet.ps1 the output shows the pwsh-7 module path in testhost and the child's own three entries. Every HeldOpenTree Fact prints 'fsutil … DisableLastAccess = 2' with 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators; Defender AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True, platform=4.18.26080.4' on the next line. The timeout Fact returned in 1018 ms, and the missing-exe Fact gave 'not read (Win32Exception …)'. The full suite at HEAD d79ce14, run after the temp-path edit, passed 870 of 870 with 0 skipped (exit 0, TEMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp). Fitness: 91 rules, all hold. I read the recipe against the code. The scanner does ask to keep last access under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (Scanner.cs:296-306), the report's core fields match the Scan helper (WindowReport.cs:217-225), and a 5.1 terminating error reaches stderr as plain text, so the 'first stderr line' reason holds. One minor defect is in what was written. The agreement Fact TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc asserts a full-line regex with `AMRunningMode=\S+`. I measured that regex rejecting 'Passive Mode', 'SxS Passive Mode' and 'EDR Block Mode', and its else-branch expects 'not read' whenever the fresh read exits 0 with no integer. On a PC where Defender runs passive, the default suite goes red, which contradicts the design's 'nothing turns red'. This PC reads Normal. Second, the C-008 test feeds an absent JSON key. I measured that the real child never produces one: a missing cmdlet property serialises as null. That is backlog. O-014, O-015 and O-016 are routed to validate-slice but need CFA armed by an administrator, so validate cannot discharge them unattended (CC-006, lesson #398). The index shows a single build attempt and no loop.

Second round: Second round: I tried to break the code and ran each suspect input. Two new defects, both minor.

1. TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath can go red on a machine where the strip works. With PSModulePath removed, Windows PowerShell 5.1 rebuilds its path from the Machine and User values; the child's entries here are exactly this PC's machine value. The Fact's regex `(?<![a-z])PowerShell\\(7\\)?Modules` also matches any foreign entry such as `…\Microsoft SQL Server\150\Tools\PowerShell\Modules\` (measured matches=True). This is the same family as round-1 m1: a default-suite Fact that asserts a machine's configuration.

2. Describe is not total, although the contract says 'Total over all inputs. It never throws'. Measured on .NET 10.0.12:
   - an escaped lone surrogate (`"\ud800abc"`) parses, then GetString throws InvalidOperationException in IsPlaceholder or Text;
   - a raw lone surrogate makes JsonDocument.Parse throw ArgumentException, which `catch (JsonException)` does not catch.

   The production line is unaffected. The real 5.1 child turns a lone surrogate into '?' (measured), and ReadOnce's catch-all guards Line. But Describe and Read both claim never to throw, and both do.

Checked and not filed:
- A 3,235-character JSON line with non-ASCII parses (non-ASCII becomes U+FFFD; counts unaffected).
- A 5.1 terminating error reaches stderr as plain text, with CRLF handled by FirstLine.
- The ProcessStartInfo.Environment removal is case-insensitive on Windows.
- Record() only prints; every HeldOpenTree measurement is taken in the fixture, so the Defender read's delay cannot disturb it.
- The recipe's Scan helper fields match WindowReport.cs, and a wrong `$base` voids the session through Control and the canary rather than misreading.

findings.claim: TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc asserts the machine-dependent shape of the line, not just the CFA value. Its regex requires `AMRunningMode=\S+`. Defender's documented AMRunningMode values include multi-word ones ('EDR Block Mode', 'SxS Passive Mode', 'Passive Mode'; recalled, this PC reads 'Normal'). I ran the regex against the line Describe builds: Normal matches=True; Passive Mode, SxS Passive Mode and EDR Block Mode all matches=False. In those modes Get-MpPreference still answers, so the fresh read succeeds, the full-format assertion runs and the default-suite Fact goes red. The else-if branch (line 62) does not check ExitCode. A fresh read that exits 0 with no integer (EnableControlledFolderAccess null on an older platform, so stdout is empty) therefore asserts 'not read (' against a line that reads 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=?', and that is red too. The design's decision is that the record 'never asserts' a machine's state and 'nothing turns red'. The builder said this Fact discharges O-001 'without asserting a machine's setting'.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderStateRecordTests.cs:55-65. Regex check run in pwsh against Describe's line format with the four AMRunningMode values. Design key_decisions: 'A machine's Defender setting is not a test outcome … On machines without Defender the line says not read and nothing turns red.'

quote.text: @"allowed apps=(\d+|hidden from non-administrators|\?); Defender AMRunningMode=\S+, RealTimeProtection=(True|False|\?), platform=\S+$", line);

findings.fix: Change `AMRunningMode=\S+` to `AMRunningMode=[^,]+` and make the else-if branch `fresh.ExitCode != 0` (or drop it). Add one Describe row with mode "EDR Block Mode" whose line passes the same regex.
findings.class_of: machine states the CFA agreement Fact turns red on

findings.claim: Case 8 ('a property is missing from the JSON') is tested only with the key removed from the object. The real child cannot produce that shape: it builds a [pscustomobject] with every key, and a property the cmdlet lacks serialises as null. Measured here with powershell.exe 5.1: `[pscustomobject]@{mode=$s.AMRunningMode; allowed=$s.NoSuchList; rtp=$s.Nope} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress` gives {"mode":null,"allowed":null,"rtp":null}. The null branch for mode, rtp and platform (Text's default arm) is correct, but no test feeds it, so a change that printed '' or 'null' for null would stay green. For the two lists, a missing property arrives as null and Count prints '0', which reads the same as an empty list. The design's 'a missing property prints as ?' is reachable only through a shape the child never emits.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderStateRecordTests.cs:234-243 removes keys; DefenderState.cs:181 maps list null to "0"; DefenderState.cs:201-208 maps a scalar null to "?" through the default arm.

quote.text: var kept = whole.RootElement.EnumerateObject().Where(p => p.Name != missing).ToDictionary(p => p.Name, p => p.Value.GetRawText());

findings.fix: Add InlineData rows that set mode, rtp, platform and enable to JSON null (via Stdout(mode: "null") and similar) and assert '?'. Record in the design note that a missing list property reads as 0.

findings.claim: O-014, O-015 and O-016 are owed to validate-slice, but none of them can be verified unattended. O-016 (the person can arm CFA) needs an administrator. O-015 (a custom folder is judged like Documents) and the trust half of O-014 (CFA judges the unsigned published exe) need CFA armed. The survey measured that the Sandbox cannot run Defender. Validate will therefore stop on obligations it cannot discharge. Lesson #398 and CC-006 say person-gated must-verify preconditions belong in filed_for_later with who=person. Design-slice imported them as validate obligations instead.
findings.evidence: The STILL OWED list (O-014/O-015/O-016, owed to validate-slice). The design's cross_domain_transfer invariants are marked must-verify. The survey measured WinDefend DISABLED, 1058, 0x800106ba in the Sandbox.
findings.fix: Re-route O-014, O-015 and O-016 to the person's run (filed_for_later, who=person, beside criteria 2 and 3). Validate can still check the part it can reach: Get-AuthenticodeSignature on artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe reads NotSigned.

findings.claim: TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath turns red on a machine where the PSModulePath strip works. With the variable removed, the 5.1 child builds its path from the Machine and User PSModulePath values. Measured: this PC's machine value is `C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules;C:\WINDOWS\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules`, which is exactly the child's last two entries. The Fact then asserts that no entry matches `(?i)(?<![a-z])PowerShell\\(7\\)?Modules`. That regex matches any `\PowerShell\Modules` entry, not only pwsh 7's. Measured: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft SQL Server\150\Tools\PowerShell\Modules\` matches=True, and SQL Server's tools add an entry of this form to the machine PSModulePath (recalled). A user-level PSModulePath that someone set for pwsh 7 also matches. On such a PC the default suite goes red although the child got no inherited path, which contradicts the design's 'nothing turns red'. This is a second member of the round-1 m1 family.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderStateRecordTests.cs:95. Measured: [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PSModulePath','Machine') against the child's printed path; regex test on three paths.
findings.fix: Build the set the strip must keep out: the entries of this process's PSModulePath minus the entries of the Machine and User values (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PSModulePath", EnvironmentVariableTarget.Machine / User)). Assert that the child's split path contains none of them, comparing without case and ignoring a trailing backslash. The mutation (strip removed) still turns it red, because the pwsh 7 entries are in that set.
findings.class_of: default-suite SL-101 Facts that turn red on a valid machine configuration

findings.claim:
Describe is not total, and Read is not never-throwing, although the design contract says 'Total over all inputs. It never throws' and the doc comments repeat it (DefenderState.cs:58, :119). Measured with System.Text.Json on .NET 10.0.12:
- stdout whose list entry or mode is an escaped lone surrogate (`"\ud800abc"`) parses, then JsonElement.GetString() throws InvalidOperationException ('Cannot read incomplete UTF-16 JSON text as string with missing low surrogate') from IsPlaceholder or Text;
- stdout carrying a raw lone surrogate makes JsonDocument.Parse(string) throw ArgumentException ('Cannot transcode invalid UTF-16 string to UTF-8 JSON text').
Only `catch (JsonException)` is there, so both escape Describe and Read. Impact today: none in the record line. Measured: the 5.1 child writes a lone surrogate as '?', and ReadOnce's catch-all would turn any escape into 'not read'. The defect is that the contract every caller and test relies on is false.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderState.cs:131-139 (parse) and :194-195 and :203 (GetString). Measured: JsonDocument.Parse and GetString on three crafted strings in pwsh on runtime 10.0.12; a 5.1 child's ConvertTo-Json of [char]0xD800 arrived as '?abc'.
findings.fix: Widen the parse catch to `catch (Exception e) when (e is JsonException or ArgumentException)`. Wrap the formatting return in try/catch (InvalidOperationException) that returns NotRead("unparsed output"). Add the two lone-surrogate strings as EmptyOrUnparsedOutputIsNotRead rows.
findings.class_of: inputs on which DefenderState.Describe throws despite its totality contract

obligations.evidence: HeldOpenTreeTests.cs Record() writes `output.WriteLine(DefenderState.Line);` on the line after the fsutil line. My detailed run shows the two lines adjacent in every HeldOpenTree Fact, and TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc passed. Its over-tight format regex is finding m1.

DefenderState.Run calls start.Environment.Remove("PSModulePath") (DefenderState.cs:73). In my run testhost's PSModulePath held the pwsh 7 entries and the child reported only its three WindowsPowerShell entries (TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath).
ANullOrEmptyListCountsAsZero feeds null and [] to both lists; Count maps Null to 0 (DefenderState.cs:181) and an empty array to its length.
AScalarListCountsAsOneNotAsItsLength feeds two bare JSON strings; Count maps String to 1 (DefenderState.cs:182).
AnArrayListCountsItsLength feeds arrays of 1, 2 and 3 entries to both lists.
TheModeIsNamedAndTheRawValueKept row ("2","AuditMode"); Enable switch at DefenderState.cs:159-167.
AnEnableValueOutsideTheKnownRangeIsKeptRawAndCalledUnknown: 7, 5, -1, 255, 1.5, "2" and true each print raw text with (unknown).
AMissingPropertyPrintsAQuestionMarkAndTheRestOfTheLineStays removes each key in turn. It feeds absent keys only, a shape the real child never emits (finding m2).

ANonZeroExitIsNotReadWithTheFirstStderrLine Theory, plus ...FromARealChild (a real 5.1 child, exit 3, stderr 'boom'). I measured that a 5.1 terminating error reaches redirected stderr as plain text, first line = message.
EmptyOrUnparsedOutputIsNotRead (9 rows, including a banner before the JSON and trailing text) and NullOutputIsNotReadEither.

AChildPastTheTimeoutIsKilledAndNotRead: real Start-Sleep 30 child with a 1 s timeout. My run printed 'returned after 1018 ms: … not read (timed out after 1 s)'. Kill(entireProcessTree:true) is at DefenderState.cs:107. That the PID is gone is not asserted (M7 waived).

AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead: the path is under AppContext.BaseDirectory, and my run printed 'not read (Win32Exception: An error occurred trying to start process …)'. No fsa-no-such-program file was left in bin.
DefenderStateRecordTests has no Trait, Skip or Explicit. OptInTraitTests and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped passed in my filtered run, and the full suite passed 870/870 with 0 skipped at HEAD.

The recipe's Scan helper drives the published exe through read-window.ps1 (default -Exe artifacts\publish\FsAnalyser.App.exe; doc step 3). Whether CFA judges that image as untrusted needs CFA armed, which no stage here can do (finding m3).

The recipe uses custom protected folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (doc steps 2 and 5). M4/O-020 (the Public\Documents fixture) was waived to SC-275, so a custom folder is still not shown to be judged like Documents.
Doc step 5 gives the cmdlet and the Windows Security UI fallback. Arming needs an administrator and was not rehearsed (doc 'Not rehearsed: every W-admin step').

DefenderState.IsPlaceholder (prefix 'N/A:', case-insensitive, after TrimStart), applied to a scalar and to any array element. The DefenderStateCorpus.json rows are P01-P09 and R01-R08. The live line on this PC reads 'allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators'.
Doc lines 71-75 (W-admin and W-user), 136-138 (the whoami Mandatory Label check throws unless Medium), 243 (Integrity column; a High row is void).

Doc step 4 (run A, CFA-off baseline), lines 100-104 (48 h back-dating before arming), Witness/Control helpers at 140-157, reading key at 249-268. The scanner asks to keep under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (Scanner.cs:296-306), so the baseline can read unchanged.
Waived to SC-275. The recipe still uses %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp fixtures.
Waived to SC-276. The .taad/fitness.yaml rule is still `\b(Set|Add|Remove)-MpPreference\b` with no (?i), over tests/** only.
Waived to SC-277. The strip is kept; the class remarks name VolumeUsageTests.GetVolumeUsed as the idiom (DefenderState.cs:17), which covers half of M6.
Waived to SC-278. Run() exposes no PID, and the timeout Fact checks only text and elapsed time.
Waived to SC-279. Step 1 lists both lists by name from W-admin; step 9 re-lists allowed apps but does not say to remove session additions or void on a match.

cases.evidence: TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc compares the line with a fresh Get-MpPreference read (0 on this PC); TheLineIsRecordedRightAfterTheFsutilLine pins the source line. The detailed HeldOpenTree run shows the two lines adjacent.

Under eng/dotnet.ps1, testhost's PSModulePath held the pwsh 7 entries (printed). TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath drives the real Run() and the child reported only WindowsPowerShell paths. The HeldOpenTree line was not 'not read'.
ANullOrEmptyListCountsAsZero InlineData("null") is fed to both lists; corpus R01 too.
AScalarListCountsAsOneNotAsItsLength feeds bare JSON strings (a long path and "R"), which count 1, not their length.
AnArrayListCountsItsLength feeds 2- and 3-element arrays; corpus R05 and R08.

AMissingPropertyPrintsAQuestionMarkAndTheRestOfTheLineStays removes the key, including mode and platform, as the row states. The real child emits a null value instead (measured), and no test feeds null (finding m2).
ANonZeroExitIsNotReadWithTheFirstStderrLine Theory (includes the 0x800106ba text) and a real 5.1 child exiting 3 with stderr 'boom'.
EmptyOrUnparsedOutputIsNotRead: empty, blank, 'not json', '{', array, null, number, banner+JSON, trailing text.
AChildPastTheTimeoutIsKilledAndNotRead: real child Start-Sleep 30, 1 s timeout; returned in 1018 ms with 'timed out after 1 s'. That the child is gone is not asserted (M7 waived).
AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead: a non-existent exe under AppContext.BaseDirectory; Process.Start throws Win32Exception, which becomes 'not read (Win32Exception: …)'.

Deferred by the design as performance only. The reason holds: `new Lazy<string>(Func)` defaults to ExecutionAndPublication (DefenderState.cs:39), and an uncached read would still print a correct line.
OptInTraitTests and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped passed in my filtered run; the full suite passed 870/870 with 0 skipped. The new class carries no Trait, Skip or Explicit.

drift: The timeout Fact runs a 30 s sleeper where the design said a 5 s one. This appears only in the O-011 claim, not under deviations. It is a strengthening: a 1 s return now proves the kill rather than a short sleep.

Run() waits up to 5 s more for the stdout and stderr pipes after the child exits (DefenderState.cs:89-90). If they do not close, the result is reported as 'timed out after 20 s' although the child exited, and the worst-case read is about 25 s, not the designed 20 s. Not declared; harmless.

The design listed two real-runner Facts. The build has five: timeout, missing exe, a real non-zero exit, PSModulePath, and the fresh-read agreement. Two are declared; the real non-zero-exit Fact (ANonZeroExitIsNotReadWithTheFirstStderrLineFromARealChild) is not.
ReadOnce wraps Read in a catch-all so the Lazy can never cache an exception. The design does not mention it, but it is consistent with the never-throw contract.
